To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in vitro platelet function tests, plasma fibrinolytics and fibrinogen concentrations are useful tools for the assessment of individual risk of thrombosis in patients with myocardial infarctions and for the selection of patients who may benefit from antithrombotics therapy.
in young survivors of acute myocardial infarctions with stable phase of coronary artery disease there are some disturbances in the hemostatic system.

the use of a new method, the determination of fibrinolytic system parameters, in addition to classical hemostasis tests, allows to identify a subgroup of young men with increased risk of coronary thrombosis after myocardial infraction, who should receive antithrombotics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of the individualized indications for the antithrombotics in the young patients after myocardial infraction.
the problem of secondary prevention in young patients after myocardial infraction.
the problem of thrombotic complications in young men after the first myocardial infarct, during the stable phase of the disease, and with the evaluation of the risk of thrombotic recurrences.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in young survivors of acute myocardial infarct the thrombotic risk is higher than in healthy subjects of the same age.
in young patients with myocardial infarctions the risk of thrombotic complications is increased, and therefore the antithrombotics should be administered.
in the group of young survivors of myocardium infarction with a period of clinical and ECG stability, the risk of thrombosis is higher than that in a group of healthy men.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the hemostatic disturbances are more frequent in young patients with myocardial infarctions, and the disturbances are more frequent and severe in patients with a history of recurrent myocardial infarct.
the young survivors of myocardinal infarction should be treated with aspirin and/or anticoaggulants.

young survivors of myocardical infarction, who are clinically stable, are at high thrombotic risk, therefore, the secondary prevention of coronary heart disease should be based on the individualized therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in the case of myocardial infarcion in young men, the risk of thrombosis is high.
the use of a combination of anticoagulant and antiplatelet drugs is more effective than either drug alone in preventing the recurrence of cardiovascular disease.
the individualization of antithrombotics is a must.
